annotation.title_clean: The Problem of Establishing Civil Liability for Harmful Effects of Smart Robots
annotation.title_en: The Problem of Establishing Civil Liability for Harmful Effects of Smart Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Alayaydeh, H.A.; Awaisheh, S.M.; Al-Taani, M.; Al-Dabbas, N.A.; Alqudah, A.M.; Awaisheh, S.M.
annotation.venue: Indian Journal of Information Sources and Services
annotation.summary_en: Jordanian legal-doctrinal article on whether smart robots can be classed as "things" or "products" under Jordanian law, drawing on French law. It tests custodian liability for things (Art. 291 of Jordan's Civil Code) and defective-product liability against harm from robots. It finds current rules inadequate and calls for dedicated legislation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Jordanian law provides no explicit legal definition of AI or smart robots
Custodian liability for objects and machines (Jordan Civil Code Art. 291; French Civil Code Art. 1242) fits autonomous robots poorly
Smart robots can be classed as products in both their physical and intangible dimensions under Jordan's consumer protection and standards laws
Autonomous robots may cause harm without any defect, which limits defective-product liability
A modern legal framework is needed to clearly allocate responsibility for harm caused by robots
